Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

constechr 0.2.0

Second release (#105). It refactors and extends v0.1.0’s functions: a public vector reader, an AOI that is always one area, clearer names, and simpler writing and template arguments. Tools install it with pak::pak("NCC-CNC/constechr@v0.2.0"). The entries for the development versions below give the detail, and the ADRs in docs/decisions/ the reasons.

Breaking changes

Removed or renamed outright, without a deprecation period, by the owner’s decision while constechr is 0.x (ADR 0026). Passing a removed argument is R’s “unused argument” error.

  • read_aoi() no longer has union: an AOI is always dissolved into one area, with no attributes (#102). To read features with their attributes, use read_layer().
  • create_wtw_planning_units() no longer has aoi_union, and its AOI must be one feature; dissolve several first, for example with read_aoi() (#102). With a one-feature AOI and the defaults, its outputs are unchanged.
  • extract_layers() and write_rasters(): the output folder argument dir is now output_dir (#109).

New functions

  • read_layer() reads one layer of a vector file or folder as sf, as stored (#104). read_aoi() reads files through it.
  • write_raster_file() writes a raster to one file at a given path, one layer or several as bands (#108, ADR 0027).

New arguments and defaults

  • rasterize_aoi()’s cells defaults to "centre" instead of being required (#106, ADR 0008). create_1km_grid() and create_wtw_planning_units() keep "touches".
  • polygonize_raster(dissolve = TRUE) merges cells into one feature per value, with values kept exact (#107).
  • create_1km_grid(), create_wtw_planning_units() and extract_wtw_natdata() gain template_file, the national template’s path within natdata_dir, defaulting to "_1km/idx.tif" as before (#110).

Other changes

  • read_aoi() stops with a clear error naming invalid geometries, instead of failing inside GEOS or passing a single invalid feature on; it does not repair them (#103). It accepts geometry collections that hold only polygons (#103), and a multi-layer source given without a layer reads its first layer, with a message (#104).
  • With datatype = NULL, a raster with no stored data type, such as one held in memory, is written in a type inferred from its values, with a message, instead of being an error (#108, ADR 0027). Where a type was found before, it is still used.
  • extract_layers() keeps layers with the same file name apart in memory (rij, rij.1) (#96, ADR 0015).
  • Argument checks shared between files are in one place (#53); no change to results or messages.

constechr 0.1.0.9009

  • create_1km_grid(), create_wtw_planning_units() and extract_wtw_natdata() gain template_file, the national template’s file within natdata_dir as a path relative to it, passed to natdata_template() as its file (#110). The default, "_1km/idx.tif", is the file they opened before, so no existing call or result changes. Another path opens a template kept elsewhere in a NAT_DATA folder, such as another version or resolution. It is the last argument of each, so positional calls keep working. When the template cannot be opened, the error names template_file and the path tried.

constechr 0.1.0.9008

  • New write_raster_file() writes a raster to one file at a given path (#108, ADR 0027): one layer, or several layers as the bands of one file, each band named after its layer. It is the writer write_rasters() already used internally, now exported with its checks: missing parent folders are created, and filename must be a single path, not inside an existing file, not a file x is read from, and not an existing file with overwrite = FALSE. Rounding (round_int) and NoData are as in write_rasters().
  • With datatype = NULL, a raster with no stored data type (held in memory, such as one made or changed in R) or with layers of different stored types is no longer an error: its data type is inferred from its values, and a message names the type and why (#108, ADR 0027). Whole numbers get the smallest integer type that holds their range without its NoData value (INT1U, INT2U or INT4U when the smallest value is 0 or more, else INT2S or INT4S); values with decimals, or beyond 32-bit integers, get FLT4S (FLT8S beyond its range); all NA gets INT1U. This applies to write_raster_file(), write_rasters() (for each file), align_raster() (for an in-memory input written to filename) and extract_layers() and extract_wtw_natdata() (for a layer with no datatype in layers, no datatype argument and no stored type, such as an .rds rij matrix, which no longer stops the call before extracting). Where a data type was found before, it is still used, so no call that worked before changes its output.

constechr 0.1.0.9007

Breaking changes

Renamed outright, without a deprecation period, by the owner’s decision while constechr is 0.x (#109, ADR 0026). Passing dir is now R’s “unused argument” error.

  • extract_layers() and write_rasters(): the output folder argument dir is now output_dir, matching constechr’s other folder arguments (natdata_dir, project_dir, tifs_dir) and no longer shadowing base::dir(). Behaviour is unchanged; only the name changes. Calls that pass the folder by position are unaffected; calls that name it (dir = "out") must use output_dir = "out". Error messages name output_dir.

constechr 0.1.0.9006

  • polygonize_raster() gains dissolve = FALSE (#107). The default is unchanged: one polygon per cell. dissolve = TRUE merges all cells with the same value into one feature per value, whether or not they touch (a value in separate patches gives one MULTIPOLYGON), ordered by value, ascending, so id numbers the values. Values are matched exactly and keep the raster’s stored type (ADR 0019); they are not rounded or compared in single precision, as terra::as.polygons()’s own dissolve = TRUE does. create_1km_grid() and create_wtw_planning_units() are unchanged.

constechr 0.1.0.9005

  • extract_layers() without dir makes repeated list names unique with make.unique() (#96, ADR 0015). Two layers with the same file name in different folders (such as species/rij.rds and habitat/rij.rds), or a layer given twice, were both named rij, so x[["rij"]] returned only the first; now they are rij and rij.1, in the order of layers. Names change only for repeated file names; written files are unaffected.

constechr 0.1.0.9004

  • rasterize_aoi()’s cells argument has a default, "centre" (cells whose centre is inside the AOI, terra’s and GDAL’s own default), instead of being required (#106, ADR 0008). No existing call changes its result, since every call had to name cells. create_1km_grid() and create_wtw_planning_units() keep their default, cells = "touches".

constechr 0.1.0.9003

  • read_aoi() checks that the AOI’s geometries are valid (sf::st_is_valid()), in the target CRS before the dissolve, and stops with a clear error naming the invalid features and why, suggesting sf::st_make_valid() (#103). Geometries are checked, not repaired. Before, an invalid AOI failed with a GEOS error in sf::st_union(), or, for a single invalid feature, was passed on as is. rasterize_aoi() and the other functions that read an AOI with read_aoi() check it too.
  • read_aoi() and create_wtw_planning_units() accept a geometry collection that holds only polygons or multipolygons, as one multipolygon of its polygons (#103). A collection holding points or lines is still an error, so nothing is dropped silently.
  • read_aoi() documents how to use the bounds of a raster or other spatial object (read_aoi(sf::st_bbox(r))), and rasterize_aoi() documents that a small part of an AOI in several parts can get no cells without a warning.

constechr 0.1.0.9002

Breaking changes

Removed outright, without a deprecation period, by the owner’s decision while constechr is 0.x (#102, ADR 0026). Passing a removed argument is an “unused argument” error.

  • read_aoi() no longer has a union argument: an AOI is always dissolved into one area (one row, one polygon or multipolygon, no attributes). To read features with their attributes, use read_layer() and sf::st_transform().
  • create_wtw_planning_units() no longer has an aoi_union argument, and requires the AOI to be one feature: an AOI of several features, accepted before, is now an error, raised before anything is written. Dissolve them first, for example with read_aoi(). aoi_file is that feature with its attributes, reprojected to the template’s CRS; a path is read with read_layer()’s reader. With a one-feature AOI and the defaults, the outputs are unchanged.

Other changes

  • create_wtw_planning_units() checks its create_1km_grid() arguments itself, before reading the AOI, so errors about them, and about the AOI, name create_wtw_planning_units() and its aoi argument.

constechr 0.1.0.9001

  • New read_layer() reads one layer of a vector file or folder as sf, as stored (#104): by name or position with layer, or the first layer by default, with a message naming it when the source has others. ... is passed to sf::st_read() (for example query). Nothing is reprojected or changed. Missing files, sources GDAL cannot open, missing layers, layer positions out of range and layers with no geometries are clear errors. It is in a new “Vector layers” family.
  • read_aoi() reads files through read_layer(). A path to a source with more than one layer and no <path>/<layer> now reads its first layer, with a message, instead of being an error. Other files read as before.

constechr 0.1.0

First release (#28). It has functions for what wtw-data-prep2 does to make a Where To Work project’s planning units and extract NAT_DATA layers for them. Tools install it with pak::pak("NCC-CNC/constechr@v0.1.0"). Each function documents its method and has known-answer tests; the entries for the development versions below give the detail, and the ADRs in docs/decisions/ the reasons.

Building blocks, with no use-case conventions:

  • read_aoi() reads an area of interest from sf or SpatVector polygons, a file or bounds, optionally reprojected and dissolved.
  • rasterize_aoi() rasterizes an AOI onto a template, onto coarser cells that nest in it, or onto a new grid, with an explicit cell rule ("touches" or "centre").
  • align_raster() puts a one-layer raster onto a template’s grid with terra::project().
  • polygonize_raster() turns each cell with a value into its own square polygon.
  • read_rij_matrix() reads a raster or a prebuilt .rds file as an rij matrix on a template.
  • clip_rij_matrix() keeps an rij matrix’s columns in an AOI raster and drops rows with no values there.
  • rij_matrix_to_raster() rebuilds rasters from an rij matrix on the AOI raster’s extent.
  • write_rasters() writes a raster’s layers to GeoTIFFs, one per layer or one multi-band file.
  • extract_layers() extracts many layers (GeoTIFFs or rij matrices) for an AOI, in memory or to files.

NAT_DATA use-case functions:

  • natdata_template() opens the national 1 km template raster, _1km/idx.tif.
  • read_natdata_metadata() reads the layer catalogue, WTW_NAT_PREP_METADATA.csv, ready for extract_layers().
  • create_1km_grid() makes an AOI’s 1 km planning units on the national template.

Where To Work (WTW) use-case functions, wtw-data-prep2’s steps 01 to 03:

  • create_wtw_project_folder() and wtw_project_folders() create a WTW project’s folders.
  • create_dataprep_template() and dataprep_columns() write its dataprep/dataprep.csv template.
  • create_wtw_planning_units() writes its aoi/aoi.shp, aoi/pu_1km.shp and aoi/pu_1km.tif.
  • extract_wtw_natdata() extracts the NAT_DATA layers into its tifs/ folder.

With their defaults, the WTW functions write the same files as wtw-data-prep2 on the test fixtures and on a real project. The main intended differences from wtw-data-prep2’s code:

  • Rules that were implicit are arguments: the AOI cell rule (cells, not a 1000 m buffer), the resampling method, data types, file names, band names and planning-unit values, with the old values as defaults.
  • Inputs are checked before anything is read or written: rasters off the template’s grid, AOIs that do not overlap it, missing files, values a data type cannot store and clashing outputs are errors that name the input, and a failed write leaves no new files.
  • Dropped features and skipped layers are named in messages, and every AOI cell that is not NA counts when clipping an rij matrix (not only values above 0).
  • Rasters are aligned with terra, not gdalwarp (ADR 0007): the output carries the template’s CRS and exact grid, and a few edge cells can differ when reprojecting.
  • Raster values keep their stored type (ADR 0019), so NCCID is an integer.
  • aoi/pu_1km_align.tif is no longer written by default (align_file writes it).

constechr 0.0.0.9018

  • create_wtw_planning_units()’s datatype argument is renamed raster_datatype, and it has two new arguments for raster_file (#79): raster_value (default 1), the value of the planning units, and raster_name (default "layer"), the name of its band, which were fixed in the code. extract_wtw_natdata() has align_name (default "layer"), the name of align_file’s band. The defaults are the old values, so the files are unchanged. As for align_value, a raster_value that raster_datatype cannot store (outside its range or its NoData value, such as 255 as INT1U) is an error before the AOI is read. Calls passing datatype must use raster_datatype; calls passing overwrite (in create_wtw_planning_units()) or round_int or later arguments (in extract_wtw_natdata()) by position must name them. Decisions in ADR 0018 and ADR 0020.

constechr 0.0.0.9017

  • extract_wtw_natdata() has two new arguments for the optional aligned planning-unit file (#76): align_value (default 1) and align_datatype (default "INT1U"), the value of the planning units in align_file and its data type, which were fixed in the code. The defaults are the old values, so results are unchanged. A value the data type cannot store (outside its range or its NoData value, such as 255 as INT1U) is an error before any layer is read. The two follow align_file, before round_int, so calls passing round_int or later arguments by position must name them. Decision in ADR 0020.

constechr 0.0.0.9016

  • New create_dataprep_template() and dataprep_columns() write the dataprep/dataprep.csv template of wtw-data-prep2’s step 01 (#27): create_dataprep_template(project_dir) writes a CSV of the columns in columns with a row of their descriptions, and returns its path. dataprep_columns() is the default, wtw-data-prep2’s eight columns and descriptions. file (relative to project_dir, default "dataprep/dataprep.csv") and overwrite (default TRUE, as today) are arguments; columns also takes column names only, or a data frame written as it is. Written with write.csv() as UTF-8, NA as empty fields. Decisions in ADR 0023. With the defaults it writes the same file as wtw-data-prep2’s create_project_folder(), byte for byte.

constechr 0.0.0.9015

  • New create_wtw_project_folder() and wtw_project_folders() are wtw-data-prep2’s step 01 folders (#26): create_wtw_project_folder() creates a WTW project folder and the folders in folders, keeping existing folders and files, and returns their paths. wtw_project_folders() is the default list, the 32 folders wtw-data-prep2’s create_project_folder() creates; with layers (a NAT_DATA catalogue from read_natdata_metadata()), the theme and weight folders are tifs/<subdir> for its layers instead, the folders extract_wtw_natdata() writes to. Decisions in ADR 0021. The dataprep/dataprep.csv template step 01 also writes is not written (it is #27).

constechr 0.0.0.9014

  • New extract_wtw_natdata() is wtw-data-prep2’s step 03 in one call (#25): natdata_template() and extract_layers() with the NAT_DATA catalogue (read_natdata_metadata(), path_column = "file"), writing each layer to <project_dir>/tifs/<subdir>/<prefix><feature>.tif with its catalogue prefix and data type. aoi_raster defaults to the project’s aoi/pu_1km.tif and also takes the raster create_wtw_planning_units() returns; layers, tifs_dir, round_int, multiband, drop_empty, overwrite and progress (a short message per layer by default) are arguments. Decisions in ADR 0020. With the defaults it writes the same tifs/ files as wtw-data-prep2’s natdata(), on the test fixtures and on a real project. Intended change: aoi/pu_1km_align.tif is no longer written by default, since nothing reads it; align_file = "aoi/pu_1km_align.tif" writes it as before (1s on the national template’s grid, INT1U).

constechr 0.0.0.9013

  • Raster values keep their stored type (#67, ADR 0019), a change to results in type, not value. rasterize_aoi() returns cell numbers as integers, the template’s values as integers when the template stores integers (an INT* data type, as NAT_DATA’s idx.tif) and doubles when it stores floats, and a constant in its own type (1L or 1). polygonize_raster() returns an integer value column when the raster stores integers (terra::is.int()) and a double column otherwise. So create_1km_grid()’s NCCID is an integer for idx.tif and for index = "cell", and create_wtw_planning_units() writes pu_1km.shp’s NCCID as an integer field, N(9,0), as wtw-data-prep2 does (it was a real field). Integers beyond R’s integer range (INT4U and larger) stay doubles.

constechr 0.0.0.9012

  • New create_wtw_planning_units() is wtw-data-prep2’s step 02 in one call (#24): create_1km_grid(), then, with project_dir, the WTW project’s aoi/aoi.shp, aoi/pu_1km.shp and aoi/pu_1km.tif (1 in every planning unit, INT1U, through write_rasters()). project_dir = NULL (the default) writes nothing. The file names (relative to project_dir, NULL to skip one), datatype and overwrite are arguments, and create_1km_grid()’s arguments pass through. aoi_union = FALSE (the default) writes the input AOI’s features and attributes in the template’s CRS, as today; TRUE writes the dissolved AOI. trim = TRUE (the default) trims both the returned raster and pu_1km.tif to the planning units, today’s extent; FALSE keeps the AOI’s box. The returned list is create_1km_grid()’s, except the raster’s extent. Decisions in ADR 0018. With the defaults it writes the same files as wtw-data-prep2’s aoi_to_grid(), on the test fixtures and on a real AOI. Differences in storage only: pu_1km.shp’s NCCID field is a real number, not an integer (same values; an integer since #67), and each square’s vertices start at another corner.

constechr 0.0.0.9011

  • New create_1km_grid() makes an AOI’s NAT_DATA 1 km planning units (#23): read_aoi() in the national template’s CRS, rasterize_aoi() on natdata_template() (cells = "touches" by default) and polygonize_raster(), returning list(aoi, aoi_raster, polygons) and writing nothing. index chooses what NCCID holds: "template", the idx.tif value (default), or "cell", the terra cell number. order chooses the polygon and PUID order: "value", sorted by NCCID (default), or "cell", terra’s cell order. Decisions in ADR 0017. With the defaults it gives the same NCCID, PUID and polygons as wtw-data-prep2’s create_1km_grid(), on the test fixtures and on a real AOI. Intended changes from that code: the raster holds the NCCIDs, not 1s, on the AOI’s extent; the polygons’ columns are NCCID, PUID, geometry (not NCCID, geometry, PUID); the AOI is dissolved into one polygon without attributes; and the “touches” rule is explicit, not reached through a 1000 m buffer and a mask.

constechr 0.0.0.9010

  • New natdata_template() opens the national 1 km template raster in a NAT_DATA folder, _1km/idx.tif by default (#22).
  • New read_natdata_metadata() reads NAT_DATA’s layer catalogue, WTW_NAT_PREP_METADATA.csv by default, keeping only active layers by default (#22). Every catalogue column is kept as it is; file (each layer’s full path) and subdir (a copy of its folder, path) are added, so the table goes straight to extract_layers(path_column = "file"). Column names are trimmed of spaces and a byte order mark. Decisions in ADR 0016. It replaces the catalogue reading in wtw-data-prep2’s natdata(), and with extract_layers() writes the same files on the test fixtures.
  • extract_layers()’s per-layer type column ("auto", "raster", "rij") is renamed format, so a catalogue’s own type column (such as NAT_DATA’s include, theme, weight) is ignored instead of failing (#22, ADR 0016). Tables with a type column for this must rename it.
  • extract_layers() gains path_column, the name of the layers column of file paths; the default, "path", keeps its behaviour (#22).

constechr 0.0.0.9009

  • New extract_layers() extracts many data layers on a template for an AOI (#21): each layer (a GeoTIFF on the template or an .rds rij matrix) is read, clipped to the AOI and rebuilt as rasters on the AOI raster’s extent, then returned in memory or, with dir, written to <dir>/<subdir>/<prefix><feature>.tif (or one multi-band <prefix><layer file name>.tif per layer with multiband = TRUE). layers is a vector of paths or a table with path and optional prefix, datatype, subdir and type columns that override the arguments per layer. Missing files, unknown types, rasters off the grid, missing data types and clashing output files are found before any layer is read; empty features and layers are dropped and named in messages; an optional progress(i, n, layer) callback reports progress. Decisions in ADR 0015. It replaces the loop in wtw-data-prep2’s natdata() and writes the same files on the test fixtures and on NAT_DATA layers. Intended changes from that code: checks before extracting, messages for dropped features and skipped layers, errors that name the layer, and output folders created as needed.
  • rij_matrix_to_raster() now builds its rasters through the same internal helpers as extract_layers(); its results are unchanged.

constechr 0.0.0.9008

  • New write_rasters() writes the layers of a raster to files: one GeoTIFF per layer, <dir>/<prefix><layer name>.tif, or all layers to one multi-band file, filename or, for a raster read from one file, <dir>/<prefix><source file stem>.tif (#20). A one-layer raster can go straight to filename. datatype = NULL uses each layer’s stored data type; round_int = TRUE rounds halves away from zero before integer types (FALSE keeps terra’s truncation) and floats are never rounded. All output paths are checked before anything is written, and files a failed call created are removed. Decisions in ADR 0014. It is the writing half of wtw-data-prep2’s rij_to_raster(), and writes the same files on the test fixtures and on NAT_DATA layers. Intended changes from that code: layer names that cannot be file names, an output that is the input’s own file, and existing files with overwrite = FALSE are errors, and a failed call leaves no new files.
  • align_raster() now writes through the same internal writer as write_rasters(); its results are unchanged.

constechr 0.0.0.9007

  • New rij_matrix_to_raster() turns the rows of an rij matrix clipped to an AOI back into rasters on the template’s grid, one layer per row, cropped to the AOI raster’s extent and held in memory (#19). Decisions in ADR 0013. It is the building half of wtw-data-prep2’s rij_to_raster(), and gives the same rasters before rounding and writing on the test fixtures and on NAT_DATA layers. Intended changes from that code: values are not rounded and no files are written (that moves to write_rasters()), an rij matrix with no rows is an error instead of returning NULL, and the national template is not copied in memory for each layer.

constechr 0.0.0.9006

  • New clip_rij_matrix() keeps the columns of an rij matrix that fall in an AOI raster on the template’s grid, and by default drops the rows with no values there, naming them in a message (#18). Decisions in ADR 0012. It replaces wtw-data-prep2’s rij_clip(), without the "AOI" and "Idx" rows, and gives the same matrices as its data rows on the test fixtures and on NAT_DATA layers. Intended changes from that code: every AOI cell that is not NA counts (not only values above 0), a row is kept if any value in the AOI is not 0 (not if its sum is above 0, which dropped negative values), an AOI of one cell works, dropped rows are reported, and an AOI raster off the template’s grid is an error.
  • The error for repeated row names in read_rij_matrix() now reads “The row names of the rij matrix from x must be unique”.

constechr 0.0.0.9005

  • New read_rij_matrix() reads one data layer as an rij matrix on a template: one row per feature, one column per template cell with data (#17). A raster on the template’s grid (a GeoTIFF path or a SpatRaster) is converted with prioritizr::rij_matrix(); a prebuilt .rds rij matrix is read as it is. type = "auto" chooses by file extension. Decisions in ADR 0011. It replaces the layer reading in wtw-data-prep2’s natdata(), which gives the same matrices on the test fixtures and on NAT_DATA layers. Intended changes from that code: a raster off the template’s grid, an .rds file with the wrong number of columns, and missing or repeated row names are errors, and a file whose extension is neither .tif, .tiff nor .rds needs type, instead of being read as an .rds file.
  • Matrix moves from Suggests to Imports; prioritizr is added to Suggests, needed only to convert rasters to rij matrices.

constechr 0.0.0.9004

  • New align_raster() puts any one-layer raster onto a template raster’s grid (CRS, extent, resolution) with terra::project() (#16). filename = NULL writes <input>_align.tif beside a file input and keeps an in-memory input in memory; resample sets the method ("near" by default); datatype = NULL uses the input file’s data type. Decisions in ADR 0007 and ADR 0010. It replaces wtw-data-prep2’s align_pu() (gdalUtilities::gdalwarp()), which gives the same cells and values on the test fixtures and on a real AOI on the national template. Intended changes from align_pu():
    • the output carries the template’s CRS (WKT), not gdalwarp’s “unknown” CRS label from a PROJ string;
    • the grid is the template’s exactly, not off by less than a nanometre;
    • when reprojecting, a few cells at the input’s edge can differ, because terra transforms exactly where gdalwarp uses an approximate transformer by default;
    • cells outside an input with no NoData value are NA, not 0;
    • values written as an integer type are rounded, not truncated, which matters only for methods other than "near";
    • an input that does not overlap the template is an error.

constechr 0.0.0.9003

  • New polygonize_raster() turns each cell of a one-layer raster that has a value into its own square polygon, as an sf layer (#15). value names the value column (default: the layer name) and id optionally adds a 1 to n column. It replaces the polygonizing in wtw-data-prep2’s create_1km_grid() (terra::as.polygons(), NCCID, PUID), which gives the same polygons, values and PUIDs on the test fixtures with value = "NCCID", id = "PUID". Intended changes from that code: equal neighbouring values are never merged (dissolve = FALSE), and polygons are in terra’s cell order (row by row from the top-left), not sorted by value, so on a template numbered from the bottom-left (such as idx.tif) the PUIDs run from the top row down.

constechr 0.0.0.9002

  • New rasterize_aoi() rasterizes an AOI onto a template raster, onto coarser cells that nest in the template’s, or onto a new grid at a given resolution (#14). cells ("touches" or "centre") is required. value is "index" (the terra cell number in the template or coarse grid, the default), "template" (the template’s own values) or a constant; drop_na drops AOI cells where the template is NA (the default); crop = FALSE returns the full grid. Decisions in ADR 0008. It replaces the rasterizing in wtw-data-prep2’s create_1km_grid() (a 1000 m buffer, terra::rasterize(), multiply by the template, mask to the AOI), which gives the same cells as cells = "touches" on the test fixtures. Intended changes from that code: the cell rule is an explicit argument instead of a buffer and terra defaults, and an AOI that does not overlap the template is an error instead of an empty result.

constechr 0.0.0.9001

  • New read_aoi() reads an area of interest from sf or SpatVector polygons, a file (shapefile, GeoPackage, GeoJSON, <gdb>/<layer>) or bounds, with optional reprojection and dissolve (#13). It replaces the inline AOI reading in wtw-data-prep2’s aoi_to_grid() and create_1km_grid() (sf::read_sf() then sf::st_transform()). Intended changes from that code: by default the AOI is dissolved into one feature without attributes (union = TRUE; union = FALSE keeps the features as before), Z and M coordinates are dropped, and the geometry column is always named geometry.
  • sf and terra move from Suggests to Imports, with assertthat and cli for argument checks.

constechr 0.0.0.9000

  • Test fixtures (tests/testthat/helper-fixtures.R) and example files in inst/extdata/ (a 10 x 10 template raster, an AOI and an rij matrix) for known-answer tests and examples (#11).
  • Initial package setup.
